title: Signal priority roadmap for cost-aware observability
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a pragmatic signal-prioritization framework and a cost-aware sampling/runout plan for inference telemetry. Goal: make investigation effective while keeping ingestion and storage costs predictable. This is a working draft — intended for feedback from eng teams and SREs.

Context / Motivation
- We’re collecting a lot of surface-level telemetry for token-serving paths; ingestion costs and dashboard sprawl are increasing.
- Teams often open 10+ dashboards when debugging a single outage; many widgets are low-signal.
- Our inference workload has highly skewed request profiles: small single-token calls + long multi-chunk chat requests. Sampling must respect both.

High-level principles
1) Prioritize user-impacting signals: SLO-facing metrics, fallback rates, error classes, and extreme tail latency.
2) Keep high-cardinality signals dormant by default; enable for scoped investigations or canary cohorts.
3) Use adaptive sampling (heat + severity) not purely random. Capture full traces for high-severity flows.
4) Make dashboards composable and small: 6–9 widgets per investigative dashboard.
5) Tie cost budgets to teams and alert when telemetry spend exceeds thresholds.

Signal Priority Matrix (ranked)
- P0 (Critical, always-on): request_latency_quantile_99, request_failure_rate, model_fallback_count, api_error_class_count, SLA_violations_per_minute, request_queue_length
- P1 (Important, always-on but low-cardinality): p50/p95 latency, tokens_per_request_histogram (aggregated), gpu_utilization_cluster, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_sizes_avg
- P2 (Investigative, sampling-on): per-tenant latency by model_variant, end-user region breakdown, request_input_size_distribution, retry_reason_breakdown
- P3 (Deep-dive, on-demand): per-request token timeline traces, full request/response samples, low-frequency perf counters (kernel-level), quantization-failure-stats

Example metric names and definitions (prometheus-style names)
- inference_request_latency_ms_bucket: histogram of request latency (ms). Used for p50/p95/p99. Tags: route, model_family, region, tier.
- inference_token_rate_per_request: gauge average tokens emitted per request over 1m window. Tags: model_family, route.
- inference_kv_cache_hit_ratio: gauge fraction of requests reusing KV prefix cache. Important for cost modeling.
- model_fallback_counter_total: counter incremented when a request falls back to cheaper or older model variant. Tags: reason, model_from, model_to.
- request_queue_depth: gauge number of inflight requests waiting for GPU.
- inference_error_type_total: counter grouped by error_class (timeout, oom, grpc_err, invalid_input).

Tracing/span conventions (lightweight + consistent)
- Root span: request_id (trace id) with service=inference-gateway.
- Span naming: <component>.<operation> e.g., gateway.parse, router.route_decision, dispatcher.batch_build, runtime.kv_lookup, runtime.decode, runtime.kernels.dispatch.
- Add tags: model_variant, tenant_id (hashed), route, batch_id (if present), sequence_length_est.
- Severity tag: derived from latency or error (low/med/high). This drives sampling policy.
- Sampling policy:
  * Always sample spans when inference_error_type_total increments for error_class=oom or timeout.
  * Sample 1% of successful requests baseline.
  * Adaptive uplift: sample additional spans for requests with latency > p95 for the associated route. If observed, increase sampling to 10% for that route for 30 minutes.
  * For experiments/canaries: support 100% sampling for targeted model_variant cohorts via route tag.

Dashboard guidelines and example widgets (investigation-focused)
- Each dashboard should open to an incident triage view: one up/down status tile, one p99 latency trend, one error waterfall, one model fallback heatmap, one queue-depth timeseries, one cost burn gauge. Keep <= 9 widgets.
- Widget queries (examples):
  * P99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) by route
  * Fallback map: sum(rate(model_fallback_counter_total[5m])) by (model_from, model_to) as heatmap
  * Queue depth: max(request_queue_depth) by instance over 1m
  * Cost burn: rolling_sum(tokens_emitted_total * cost_per_token_model_variant) over 1h (note: cost_per_token is a derived constant per model)

Sampling budget algorithm (simple bank model)
- Each team gets an observability spend budget (tokens_ingested_equivalent) per month. Telemetry ingestion converted to equivalent units to compare against compute budgets.
- Budget consumption rules: full traces cost X, metric series cost Y per minute sampled, logs cost Z per MB.
- System behavior on budget breach: 1) notify team 2) automatically reduce P2 sampling by 50% (fallback to 0.5% baseline) 3) block new high-cardinality dashboards until remediation plan submitted.

Storage / retention recommendations
- Metrics: keep full-resolution (10s) for 30d, roll up to 1m for 90d, and 1h for 365d.
- Traces: keep full traces for 7d (all high-severity + sampled), index trace metadata for 30d. Store archived trace payloads for 365d but cold.
- Logs: keep error-level logs 30d, debug sampling at 7d unless on-demand snapshot.

Operational runbook excerpts (triage flow)
1) Pager triggers -> open incident dashboard (triage view).
2) Check p99 latency and error type distribution. If p99 spikes but no error class, move to sampling uplift for the affected route.
3) If model_fallback_counter increased, cross-check rollout matrix and model versions.
4) If queue_depth > threshold, check autoscale signals and GPU utilization, and consider emergency capacity burst (dedicated).

Dashboard hygiene playbook (for owners)
- Owners: every dashboard must have an owner tag and a monthly review check-in (quick 10-min note).
- Prune: remove dashboards not viewed in 90d or with >25% stale queries.
- Standardize naming: [team] / [route] / [investigation-type] / [view]

Open questions and trade-offs
- How aggressive to be with cardinality limits for tenant_id and model_variant? (hashed tenant_id helps, but high-card routes still expensive).
- Do we want a centralized cost-sim UI for teams to see telemetry spend per dashboard? (recommended).
- Retention vs compliance: enterprise customers may require different retention windows — need per-tenant policy plumbing.

Next steps (action items)
- Aisha: propose final P0/P1 metric list and submit to obs-steering by 2024-03-08.
- Liam: prototype adaptive uplift controller in staging (JIRA-OBS-1227) — target: end of March.
- Sofia: wireframe small triage dashboard template and owner checklist — handoff to design by 2024-03-01.
- Rajiv: cost model for telemetry units and budget enforcement prototype.

Notes to reviewers (quick)
- This is intentionally pragmatic — we’re balancing signal coverage against cost. Expect refinement after a two-week pilot on high-traffic routes.
- Please add comments inline or ping in #obs-runbook-review.

Rough scratchpad / brainstorm fragments (copied from meeting)
- could we tag trace samples with quantization_config_id to debug perf regressions?
- consider 'hot-route' label when a route hits sustained >5x baseline traffic for 10m — auto-uplift sampling for 15m
- dashboard card idea: 'investigation time to first actionable insight' metric (tracking human time)

End of doc
